body:
The maintainer hit this on 2026-11-13 (in chat): "The setup things where we carry stock between setups for rest machining is giving a strange error" and "whole idea is that stock IS getting turned between setups."

What he saw (Face2 in Setup2, stock source "what Setup1 leaves behind", Setup2 holding the part turned X -90°):

```
generate failed: could not generate the toolpath: Face2: invalid machining parameters: Face2: this operation reads the stock earlier setups left, and that stock cannot be carried into its setup: carrying the machined stock from setup 'Setup1' into setup 'Setup2': 'Setup2' holds the part turned X -90°, Y 0°, Z 0° from how 'Setup1' holds it, and the stock simulation can carry machined stock only through a flip over X or Y or a quarter turn about Z (turns that keep the tool axis vertical) - any other turn would have to re-sample the stock and lose its detail
```

Priority raised from P8 to P4 (work the maintainer asked for, in his words above): a second setup that stands the part on its side is the ordinary case for carried stock, so the refusal blocks the feature's main use. Until this lands the workaround is to give Setup2 its own stock instead of the carried one.

Two things owed here: the side-on carry itself (a re-sample that never leaves the carried stock smaller than the real one, so rest machining cannot run into uncut material), and a shorter message for whatever turns stay refused.
